hints.title: Inverted Index Position Preprocessing
hints.text: Precomputing the sorted index positions of every unique string allows repeated queries to be answered in linear time relative to word occurrences.

hints.title: Two Pointers Across Sorted Offset Lists
hints.text: Traverse the two sorted position sequences simultaneously with two pointers. Update the minimal absolute difference and advance the pointer with the smaller index value.

hints.title: Merge Traversal Blueprint
hints.text: Initialize pointers i = 0 and j = 0 for the position lists. At each step, record abs(list1[i] - list2[j]). If list1[i] < list2[j], increment i; otherwise increment j. Return the minimum distance found.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: K1, K2: frequencies of queried words
complexity.notes: Constructor runs in O(N); each query runs in linear time with respect to word frequencies.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning the original words list on each query incurs O(N) cost per repeated call.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Trading O(N) space for index arrays accelerates frequent distance queries.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Optimal two-pointer progression over sorted index lists.
